::: {.why}
You have a year of measured results on exactly these questions, which means every answer can be a number from your own work rather than a textbook statement, and that is what distinguishes the answer.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Answer ten machine learning questions in ninety seconds each, citing your own measured numbers where you have them.
- State the audit result from milestone 7 as a two-sentence answer.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Ninety seconds each, recorded, with the rule that where you have your own number you use it. Purging and embargoing, the seed variance result, the effective sample size correction and the audit verdict are all things you measured, and citing them is far stronger than describing the technique.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Prepare the follow-up you will get: an interviewer who hears that boosting did not beat ridge will ask why, and the answer has to be specific rather than a shrug about signal to noise. Write the three-part answer covering the effective sample size, the turnover, and the fact that the interactions were not there.
:::
:::

## Resources

- [Gu, Kelly & Xiu (2020) — Empirical Asset Pricing via Machine Learning](https://dachxiu.chicagobooth.edu/download/ML.pdf) [paper]{.res-kind}
- [Stanford CS229 — Machine Learning, main lecture notes (PDF)](https://cs229.stanford.edu/main_notes.pdf) [reference]{.res-kind}

## Deliverable

::: {.deliverable}
Ten recorded machine learning answers citing your own measured numbers, plus the prepared three-part follow-up.
:::

## Checkpoint

::: {.checkpoint}
Standard k-fold is wrong on financial data. Give two reasons, the fixes, and the number from your own work that shows the fix mattered.
:::
